# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/game/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/game/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/game/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   listed in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through
   `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`). A test
   asserts no editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through that
   module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
5. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
6. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` and the generated per-storyline
   docs/SVGs (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`); `npm run storylines:graph --
   --format json --check`, `npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and
   `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` pass. Edits that touch a
   hand-written documented row surface an explicit "manual documentation update
   required" result naming the doc-drift check. Covered by tests.
7. **Concurrency guard** — if `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load,
   the editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
8. **Game build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the
   production game bundle; verified by a build/test assertion (e.g. the editor
   entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts` graph).
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `src/README.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — the editor must reuse the existing transactional,
  self-validating author operations; it must not introduce a second way to edit
  `src/card-data.csv`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`vite-node`/Vitest/
  Playwright toolchain.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — the manifest/mmd generators must stay
  timestamp-free; the existing drift test must continue to pass.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Backward compatibility** — CSV schema/column order and legacy
  `hasChoices`/accept/reject semantics must be preserved; the C1 regression
  harness must stay green.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to
  players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — richer option semantics (conditional/cost-gated effects,
  `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) are out of scope; the editor edits today's two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Manifest + schema** — `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` (generated,
  deterministic, 5 storyline ids, 71 nodes, 15 edges, 1 cycle) and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` (draft-07, `additionalProperties:
  false`).
- **Graph export** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` with
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json` and a `--check` drift
  guard; committed `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`.
- **Transactional author API** — `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (CLI
  `npm run storylines:author`, `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`): builds the
  edited CSV in memory, loads it through the typed model and validates **before**
  writing; `--dry-run` and `--csv <path>` supported.
- **Validator** — `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (`validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`), cycles informational, `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in.
- **Model/seam** — `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (`compileStorylineFromEvent`,
  `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`, `resolveStorylineOption`,
  `pushChainCard`); CSV authoring keeps the two-way representation.
- **Stack** — Vite + Phaser + Electron; scripts run under `vite-node` because
  the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query.
- **Gap** — no interactive editor; the only graph view is the static generated
  Mermaid/JSON plus the per-storyline SVG pages rendered by
  `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`,
  completed in `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). Nothing can edit through a UI.
- **Reusable pieces for the editor** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` exports
  `filterManifestByStoryline`, `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`,
  `describeEventImpact` and `describeChoiceRouting` (per-storyline grouping and
  labels); `src/CsvChecksum.ts` exports `computeCsvChecksum` (CSV change
  detection, already used for card-art regeneration); `validate-storylines.ts`
  exports `formatStorylineReport` / `storylineReportToJson` (report rendering).
  The committed manifest currently holds 5 storylines, 71 nodes, 15 edges and
  1 cycle.

## Desired change

1. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   modules.
2. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
3. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.
4. **Stay in sync** — regenerate the committed mmd/manifest after accepted edits
   and guard against concurrent external CSV edits.
5. **Document and test** — authoring walkthrough for the editor, unit tests for
   the bridge/view-model and a browser round-trip test.

**Recommended slice order for planning** (epic, per Q2 = A): (S1) host +
read-only viewer; (S2) write bridge + preview/validate; (S3) curated edit forms;
(S4) storyline management + docs/tests polish. The `plan` skill will formalise
the children and dependencies.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** entry point (`vite-node`).
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` (or a Vite dev-server plugin) —
  **new** host + API bridge.
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — **new** thin wrapper over
  `storyline-author.ts`, `validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/` (or `tools/storyline-editor/`) — **new** editor
  UI (HTML entry + TS view-model/graph rendering).
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`, `src/CsvChecksum.ts`,
  `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **reuse** read-only helpers (manifest
  filtering/labels, CSV checksum, validation report rendering); do not
  reimplement any of them.
- `./package.json` — add the `storylines:editor` script.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — **edit** tooling/authoring sections.
- `src/README.md` — **edit** script and CSV-column references.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.test.ts` — **new** bridge/view-model tests.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.browser.test.ts` — **new** Playwright UI test.
- `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`,
  `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` — generated artefacts (regenerated on
  accepted edits; confirm with `npm run storylines:graph -- --format json
  --check` and `npm run storylines:graph -- --check`).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" (epic, completed/in_review) — the
  parent that shipped the validator, graph/manifest export and authoring helper
  this editor builds on; its roadmap entry in
  `docs/game/storylines.md` §10 is the seed for this work item.
- **MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ** — "Storyline authoring helper CLI" (completed) — the
  transactional write API the editor wraps.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — the manifest/schema/generator the viewer reads.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — "Static validator & npm gate" (completed) — the
  validation feedback surfaced in the editor.
- **MS-0MUMP92O9002772U** — "Storyline behaviour regression harness" (completed)
  — must stay green after editor changes.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — "Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the
  docs build" (completed) — adjacent read-only visualisation. Shipped
  `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` + `npm run storylines:graph:svg`, the
  per-storyline pages under `docs/game/storylines/` and
  `docs/game/storyline-incident-index.md`; its server-side Playwright/mermaid
  renderer is docs-only, but its per-storyline grouping conventions should be
  matched by the interactive viewer.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — "Extend storyline options with conditional and
  cost-gated effects" (open) — future option model; explicitly out of scope here,
  but the editor's form model should not preclude it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "visual editor" can balloon into a full graph editor;
  *mitigation:* slice order (viewer → bridge → forms → management) and keep
  direct-manipulation graph editing out of the accepted first increments.
- **Write-path risk** — a browser UI could grow its own CSV writer;
  *mitigation:* AC4 enforces the author-API-only path with a test.
- **Concurrency risk** — external CSV edits during an editor session could be
  overwritten; *mitigation:* AC7 hash/mtime guard.
- **Build-leak risk** — the editor entry could be bundled into the game;
  *mitigation:* AC8 build exclusion test.
- **`?raw` import constraint** — the card model imports the CSV via Vite `?raw`,
  so the bridge must run under `vite-node`/Vite middleware rather than plain
  Node; *mitigation:* the host builds on the existing toolchain (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — "storylines" means the Main Street incident event-chain
  system; no other storyline implementation exists in the repo.
- **Assumption** — the editor is a local developer/content tool; hostability
  outside a repo checkout is not required.
- **Assumption** — the editor's first increments target the shipped two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model; multi-way/programmatic options remain out of scope.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Answered (producer, round 1 — 2026-10-01, interactive reply)

- **Q1 — Delivery form / host.** Where should the editor live and how is it
  launched? Options: (A) in-repo local web tool; (B) in-game developer overlay;
  (C) standalone Electron tool. **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer:
  A — in-repo local web tool** launched with `npm run storylines:editor`, built
  on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain and writing only through the
  existing author API. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Work-item shape & first increment.** Options: (A) epic decomposed into
  vertical slices; (B) single feature; (C) read-only MVP only.
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — epic**, decomposed into
  vertical slices (viewer → write bridge → edit forms → storyline management +
  docs/tests). The work item's `issueType` was set to `epic`. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Editing interaction model.** Options: (A) curated form/guided editor;
  (B) direct-manipulation graph editor; (C) both (form first, graph later).
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — curated form/guided
  editor**, with diff/preview and validate-before-write; no free-form canvas
  manipulation. Source: interactive reply.

### Answered (repo research — no interactive reply needed)

- **Q0 — Write path.** The editor must use the existing transactional author
  API (`src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`: `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`)
  and must not add a second CSV edit path. Evidence: the author module already
  validates in memory before writing; the seed states "write edits back through
  the same transactional, self-validating author operations".
- **Q0b — Artefacts.** After an accepted edit, regenerate
  `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` via
  `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`; the existing `--check` drift guard and
  doc-drift test must pass. Evidence: `docs/game/storylines.md` §5/§7.
- **Q0c — Stack constraint.** The editor host must run under Vite/`vite-node`
  because the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw`
  query. Evidence: the `storyline-author`/`storyline-graph`/`validate-storylines`
  CLIs are all `vite-node` entry points.

### Open questions

- None. All blocking questions are answered (Q1–Q3, producer); the epic scope
  and slice order are set above.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** – Synergy tooltop (completed)
- **MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI** – Reduce time upcoming event is shown (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMO3BDE000QDXJ** – Test review: apply transferred clean-ups from the core test-suite audit (in-progress)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: author, authoring, back, cli, command (+33 more)
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — matched: author, authoring, back, command, deferred (+25 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: author, back, cli, command, deferred (+24 more)

# Intake Brief: Static docs site for local browsing (VitePress)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from MS-0MUNB54KU005084C as the deferred option (B). Producer
> answers 2026-10-17: still wanted (Q1=A); **navigation-first** use case
> (Q2=A); **local dev tool only**, no CI publishing (Q3=B).

## Headline

Add a VitePress static docs site over the existing `docs/game/` and
`docs/dev/` trees so developers and content authors can browse the docs with
sidebar navigation and rendered Mermaid locally (`npm run docs`); no CI
publishing is required.

## Problem statement

The repo ships docs as a flat, two-tree Markdown forest (`docs/game/`,
`docs/dev/`). Without a site, readers must navigate raw files and there is no
sidebar nav, no search, and no unified landing page. Mermaid fences in docs
(`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `the-build-gdd.md`) render only with a
Mermaid-aware viewer. A static docs site fixes browsing and renders Mermaid at
build time.

## Users

- **Developers** — need to browse game + dev docs with nav/search while
  working on the codebase.
  - *"As a developer, I want a docs site with sidebar navigation, so I can
    find the right doc faster without guessing file paths."*
- **Game designers / content authors** — need the gameplay reference plus the
  storyline graphs readable in place.
  - *"As a content designer, I want Mermaid diagrams rendered in the docs
    page, so the storyline shape is visible without a Mermaid tool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Docs site generator** — `vitepress` (MIT) is added as a devDependency
   and a `npm run docs` script serves the docs site locally
   (`vitepress dev docs`); the site root is `docs/` and covers both the
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/` trees with sidebar navigation.
   *Metric: `npm run docs` starts a local server; `npm run docs:build`
   (vitepress build/docs) exits 0 and emits a static site.*
2. **Navigation** — a sidebar (`.vitepress/config.ts`) lists the `docs/game/`
   and `docs/dev/` documents with clear audiences; every top-level `.md` in
   both trees is reachable from the nav (no orphaned docs).
   *Metric: a test asserts every `.md` under `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/` is
   covered by the sidebar config.*
3. **Mermaid rendering** — mermaid code fences in docs render to visible
   diagrams in the built site; the existing committed storyline SVGs
   (`docs/game/assets/storyline-graph-*.svg`) remain usable and are linked or
   embedded as today.
   *Metric: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and `the-build-gdd.md`
   render with visible diagrams in the built site.*
4. **No link breakage / no migration** — existing files stay in place under
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/`; existing relative links between docs keep
   working; the `docs-path-drift` guard test stays green (no
   `docs/main-street/` or `example-games/main-street/` strings in the new
   VitePress config).
   *Metric: full suite passes including `docs-path-drift.test.ts`.*
5. **Testing/validation** — a test validates the docs build config (nav
   coverage + no forbidden paths), and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages workflow, no docs CI job
   (Q3=B). `docs` scripts are for local use; the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is untouched.
- **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` (MIT) and any new plugin must be
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
- **devDependency only** — the docs toolchain must not enter the game bundle.
- **No reorganisation** — files stay under `docs/game/` / `docs/dev/`; the
   two-tree structure and `docs/README.md` index remain.
- **Drift guard** — new VitePress files under `docs/` must not contain
   `example-games/main-street/` or `docs/main-street/` (scanned by
   `docs-path-drift.test.ts`).
- **Determinism/coverage** — the nav-coverage test must be stable and fast
   (no Playwright/browser requirement for the unit suite).

## Existing state (repo research)

- No docs-site generator present: devDeps include `vite`, `vitest`,
   `playwright`, `mermaid`, `sharp`, `tsx`, `vite-node`, but **no
   `vitepress`/`docusaurus`/`mkdocs`** anywhere in the repo or `core/`.
- `docs/` is plain Markdown: `docs/README.md` index, `docs/game/` (11 files +
   `storylines/` (5) + `assets/` with 5 storyline SVGs), `docs/dev/` (21 files +
   `assets/` (9) + `analysis/`).
- Mermaid fences exist in `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (:162),
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (:207, :617); the storyline graph
   ships as committed SVGs under `docs/game/assets/`.
- `docs-path-drift.test.ts` scans every text file under `docs/` for
   forbidden legacy paths; a `.vitepress/config.ts` (or `.mjs`) is a `.ts`
   text file and will be scanned — it must avoid those strings.
- Node v22.22.1 (VitePress requires Node ≥18 — satisfied).
- `.gitignore` has `dist/` and `dist-electron/`; VitePress build output
   (`docs/.vitepress/dist`) must be ignored (add `.vitepress` or
   `docs/.vitepress/dist`).

## Desired change

1. Add `vitepress` (devDependency) and a `docs` npm script.
2. Add `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` with sidebar nav for both trees
   (or `.mjs` if TS config is awkward with the repo's toolchain — prefer
   `.ts` since Vite toolchain is already TS).
3. Theme/plugin for Mermaid rendering (e.g. via the `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`
   or a mermaid pre-render step) so mermaid code fences become visible
   diagrams in the built site.
4. Add a nav-coverage test (`tests/main-street/`) asserting every top-level
   `.md` in both trees appears in the sidebar config, plus the drift-guard
   string check on the new config files.
5. Update `docs/README.md` (or add `docs/index.md`) to note the docs site and
   the `npm run docs` command.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — add `vitepress` devDependency + `docs` / `docs:build` npm
  scripts.
- `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` — **new** VitePress config (title, sidebar,
  mermaid plugin).
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/…` and/or mermaid plugin wiring — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/docs-site-nav.test.ts` — **new** nav-coverage + drift-
  string test.
- `.gitignore` — ignore `docs/.vitepress/` build output.
- `docs/README.md` and/or new `docs/index.md` — site introduction + `npm run
  docs` command.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid→SVG) — completed (v0.1.19); this item is its deferred option (B).
- **MS-0MUYLLYX80090370** — Link & document the rendered storyline graph — completed; embedded the SVG in the canonical doc and documented regeneration.
- **MS-0MUZK0OWJ000PQ2D** — Restructure documentation (two-tree split) — established `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/`.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths — owner of the `docs-path-drift` guard.
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked) — may eventually consume the docs-rendered graphs.

## Assumptions

- The docs site is **local-only** (Q3=B): no CI build or Pages publishing is
  added; if publishing is wanted later it is a follow-up item.
- Navigation is the primary need (Q2=A); Mermaid fences are rendered in the
  built site (client-side rendering acceptable — see risk) and do not replace
  the committed `.mmd`/SVG pipeline.
- `nodemon`/live-reload behaviour from VitePress dev server is fine; no
  custom theme is needed beyond Mermaid support.

## Risks

- **Toolchain adoption (LOW–MED).** VitePress is Vite-native (repo already
  uses Vite), but its config adds a new docs toolchain. *Mitigation:*
  devDependency only; config kept small; no bundler changes.
- **Mermaid rendering approach (MED).** `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` renders
  client-side in the browser by default, not at build time; the item title
  says "at build time". *Mitigation:* either pre-render server-side (run the
  existing `mermaid` + Playwright render step during `docs:build`) or accept
  client-side rendering for the local dev use case (Q3=B); record the choice
  in the item at implementation.
- **Drift-guard interference (LOW).** New `.vitepress` files are scanned by
  `docs-path-drift.test.ts`. *Mitigation:* keep the forbidden strings out of
  new config; nav test covers coverage.
- **Scope creep risk.** Full-text search, versioning/multi-version docs,
  CI publishing, i18n, custom theming → out of scope; record as separate
  work items if requested.
- **Test determinism (LOW).** Nav test must not require a browser; keep it a
  pure config-scan unit test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Still wanted?** Now that the minimal render step is shipped, is the
  larger static docs site still desired?
  - Options: (A) Still want it; (B) No longer needed.
  - **Recommended: (B).** Original problem solved by MS-0MUNB54KU005084C.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — still build the static docs
    site. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Primary use case?**
  - Options: (A) Better navigation/structure; (B) Mermaid-at-render for all
    docs; (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — navigation-first; Mermaid
    rendering at build time remains in the title/scope but is not the sole
    driver. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Target audience / delivery?**
  - Options: (A) Internal/CI only (Pages); (B) Local dev tool (`npm run
    docs`); (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (B)** — local dev tool only; **no CI
    publishing**. Source: interactive reply.

> All three answers recorded in comment MS-C0MVBVDIK0006YSM7.

# Intake Brief: Residual Expensive-Tier Branching Upgrades Below Pick-Rate Target

**Work item:** MS-0MV035PRV002QDG4 · `task` · `low`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)

## Headline

Two expensive-tier level-0 branching upgrades (`upg-drive-in`, cost 700; `upg-wellness-center`, cost 900) remain at or near 0% M1 pick rate on the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with higher-weighted upgrades. This task raises their draw-weight (or adjusts cost/incomeBonus) to reach ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% or breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.

## Problem statement

The upgrade-deck composition lever (MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W) added `drawWeight` values to the upgrade-deck: the four level-2 capstones and their level-1 prerequisites received weight boosts (2–3× baseline), but the remaining level-0 branching upgrades — `upg-drive-in` (Cinema, cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (Day Spa, cost 900) — were left with no `drawWeight` (baseline = 1). These two cards compete for the single upgrade slot in the market against weighted cards (drawWeight 2–3), so their market appearance rate is too low to achieve meaningful adoption. The previous rebalance (MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M) left them unchanged to avoid over-tuning the market composition.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the expensive-tier branching path (Cinema → Drive-In, Day Spa → Wellness Center) to be a viable investment option alongside the IMAX/Resort-Spa standard path and the multiplex/luxury-retreat capstone chain.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a balanced economy where all upgrade paths are reachable, with measurable Monte Carlo evidence.
- **Developer** — wants card-data-only changes (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight); no engine modifications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** Before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 pick rate for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. **Target met.** A card-data-only change (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight) lifts both `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` to ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) below 5% M1 and without breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.
3. **Tests pass.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Card data only** — no engine-rule changes. Modify `cost`, `incomeBonus`, and/or `drawWeight` in `src/card-data.csv` (or equivalent template).
- If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable without regressing capstones or breaking the difficulty ladder, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

## Existing state

- **CSV values (current):**
  | Card | Cost | incomeBonus | drawWeight | requiredLevel | targetBusiness |
  |------|------|-------------|------------|---------------|----------------|
  | upg-drive-in | 700 | 200 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-wellness-center | 900 | 250 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-imax | 700 | 300 | 2 | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-resort-spa | 900 | 350 | 2 | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-grand-bakehouse | 900 | 350 | 3 | 1 | Bakery |
  | upg-restaurant | 1400 | 550 | 3 | 1 | Diner |
  | upg-multiplex | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Cinema |
  | upg-luxury-retreat | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Day Spa |

- `drawWeight` is read from CSV column 54 into `UpgradeCard` templates and applied at market-refill time (see `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` / `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` / `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`).
- The `drawWeight` mechanism: absent → weight 1; the weighted selection at refill time uses cumulative weights.
- **Related completed work:**
  - MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (task, high)
  - MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W — Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (feature, high)
  - MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption (feature, high)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Modify `drawWeight` column for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`; optionally adjust `cost`/`incomeBonus`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — Template loading; verify `drawWeight` plumbing is correct.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-draw-weight.test.ts` — Existing draw-weight tests; add regression tests for the new values.
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` — Run `--seed-prefix mc-balance --strategy greedy --maxTurns 60 --seeds 200 --sweep` for Easy/Medium/Hard evidence.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Monte Carlo engine; no changes expected.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** — Parent context: the 5-turn payback rebalance left upgrades under-valued; this is the residual fix.
- **MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W** — Established the `drawWeight` mechanism and boosted the level-1/level-2 chain cards; `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` were intentionally left at baseline weight.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** — Cost tuning that preceded the draw-weight mechanism; established that cost alone cannot solve reachability.

# Test-failure: heavy Monte-Carlo and deploy-build cases time out under load

## Summary

Several CPU-bound test cases in the `unit` project run close to (or beyond)
their per-test `testTimeout`, so the full suite turns red on a busy host even
though every assertion passes. They need the same explicit headroom that the
peer Monte-Carlo file already uses.

## Evidence

Observed during the MS-0MV8KSPFK006HTXG epic (F3I worktree, commit
`432e3b24`), full-suite runs on a loaded host (load average 10–33, 16 cores):

```
FAIL |unit| tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts > AC1 — Deterministic head-to-head execution > should run ≥200 seeds in the batch harness
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
 ❯ tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts:78:3

FAIL |unit| tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts > MonteCarloRunSummary — Community Favour usage counters > records integral, non-negative counters on every canonical greedy run
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
 ❯ tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts:22:3
```

Re-observing while validating this item (load average ~24) also surfaced the
same class of failure in the deploy build suite, which was blocking the
full-suite gate:

```
FAIL |unit| tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts > production pages base derivation > derives /tce-main-street/ ... 
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts:64:3
```

Both Monte-Carlo files pass on a quiet run (dev HEAD, all 5833 assertions
green); the `≥200 seeds` case sits at ~8–12 s against a 15 s ceiling, and
`favour-usage-metrics` runs 200 seeds × 60 turns per case, so CPU contention
pushes either over the limit. The same contention also produced a
`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` unhandled error that made a
fully-passing run exit non-zero.

## Root cause

CPU-bound simulation loops sized at 200 seeds are inherently near the 15 s
unit default; full in-process production `vite build` cases measure 73–270 s
under load. Neither set declares adequate explicit per-test headroom.

## Precedent

`tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` already declares
`}, 120_000)` for its 200-seed cases, and `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`
runs 60 s+ per file. The failing files are the outliers.

## Scope note (deploy build files)

The deploy-build timeout fix was triaged as MS-0MVFSWC5Z000013W and is
delivered in this same commit: the two changes are mutually required for a
single green full-suite run (each worktree forked from `dev` only sees the
other's absence), so they land atomically. The item remains the tracked
record for the deploy-file failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 200-seed Monte-Carlo case in `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts`
   that currently runs close to the limit declares an explicit per-test
   timeout of at least 60 s (matching the 120 s precedent in
   `monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`).
2. Every 200-seed × 60-turn case in `tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts`
   declares an explicit per-test timeout of at least 60 s.
3. Every full-build case in `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts` and
   `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts` declares an explicit per-test
   timeout of at least 300 s (shared `BUILD_TEST_TIMEOUT` constant; 600 s
   adopted after measuring ~270 s per build under load).
4. No assertions, fixture data, or simulation/build parameters change — the
   timeout is the only behavioural difference (beyond the explicit-limit
   declaration).
5. `npm run build` succeeds and the full suite passes via the test skill
   (`run_tests.py --scope full`).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/favour-usage-metrics.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts`

# Test-failure: heavy production-build deploy tests time out at their 120 s per-test ceilings under load

## Summary

`tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts` and (sibling risk)
`tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts` each run full in-process `vite build`
per test case. Under host/CI load a single build takes 73–120 s, so the
120 000 ms per-case ceiling was itself the failure: observed via the
MS-0MVFQ5ODR001R7U2 finish gate (load average ~24/16 cores) where
`pages-base-derivation.test.ts > derives /tce-main-street/ ...` timed out at
120 000 ms while its siblings took 91 s / 73 s and `vite-base-gating` passed
at 116 s — within 4 s of the same ceiling. All assertions pass; the failure
is headroom-only.

## Evidence

```
FAIL |unit| tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts > production pages base derivation > derives /tce-main-street/ from package.json and gives the page a Main Street title
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts:64:3
```

## Root cause

Real production builds are inherently 70–120 s under load; the explicit
120 s per-test timeout (`}, 120_000)`) leaves no margin — CPU contention
pushes a single case over the limit, and the run also surfaces
`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` (birpc 60 s default RPC
timeout) unhandled errors on fully-passing workers.

## Scope

Both heavy deploy build files get the same explicit headroom (300 s), so the
failure cannot merely migrate to the sibling file (`vite-base-gating` was at
116 s / 120 s ceiling).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every full-build case in `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts` and
   `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts` declares a per-test timeout of at
   least 300 s (shared `BUILD_TEST_TIMEOUT` constant).
2. No assertions, fixture data, or build parameters change — the timeout is
   the only behavioural difference.
3. `npm run build` succeeds and the full suite passes via the test skill
   (`run_tests.py --scope full`).

## Key Files

- `tests/deploy/pages-base-derivation.test.ts`
- `tests/deploy/vite-base-gating.test.ts`
